messages.author: 8078800b7ede70d2
messages.subject: Simple ggplot2 question (barplot)
parts:
How can I produce this kind of graph using ggplot2?

> dput(dat)
structure(list(`0` = c(24L, 32L, 31L), `1` = c(20L, 14L, 17L),
`2` = c(6L, 3L, 2L), `3` = c(0, 1, 0)), row.names = c(NA,
3L), .Names = c("0", "1", "2", "3"), class = "data.frame")
> revmat <- function(mat, ...) {
+ mat[nrow(mat):1, ncol(mat):1]
+ }
> barplot(revmat(as.matrix(dat)), horiz=T, xlim=c(0, 100), legend=T)
> box()
>

-J

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Simple ggplot2 question (barplot)
parts: Dear Johannes,
Convert your dataset to a long format and then it easy.

library(ggplot2)
dat$ID <- rownames(dat)
molten <- melt(dat, id.vars = "ID")
ggplot(molten, aes(x = variable, y = value, fill = ID)) + geom_bar() + coord_flip()

HTH,

Thierry
